gapAssessment.question: does it fully resolve concurrency/recovery or hide an authorization/budget/TCB gap
gapAssessment.answer: concurrency and recovery are resolved within stated premises; two gaps are disclosed implementation obligations, one is an actual specification hole, one is an undisclosed side effect
gapAssessment.authorization: disclosed but undefined — every protection is downstream of creator eligibility, which is given only as an exclusion list plus 'native first-party host's admitted persistent first-write invocation'; the model supplies a boolean premise (probe P6c). See RF-1.
gapAssessment.budget: asserted against an owner that does not exist for this act — §2 cites 'the creating invocation's authoritative budget' but the authoritative budget is operation/installation-scoped and there is no installation yet; the model has no budget concept (probe P6b). See RF-3.
gapAssessment.tcb: honestly bounded — qualified primitives required, no overwrite fallback, no portability claim from one host, no rollback/copy detection claimed. Concrete consequence: the product today has exclusive no-replace publication for regular files only (publish_new_regular), with no directory-publication primitive and no directory-barrier receipt type, so two native capabilities remain unimplemented.

requiredFindings.finding: Creator eligibility is defined only as a list of exclusions plus a phrase; it is the load-bearing safety element of the whole unit.
requiredFindings.required: State a positive checkable predicate: which admitted owners (execution principal, launch/core closure, platform/filesystem profile, native persistent first-write surface) are consulted, in what order, and what typed non-forgeable receipt their conjunction yields. Keep the exclusion list, but it cannot be the definition.

requiredFindings.finding: The new directory-publication durability recursion has no defined base case. '…continue up to the already admitted durable ancestor' never says what first establishes one, while the same section allows this act to create the fixed ancestors, so on a fresh machine the chain can be entirely self-created and the rule recurses without a stopping condition. Three different implementations are equally consistent with the text.
requiredFindings.required: Name the durability base (the account-derived directory this act does not create) and state that every component this act creates owes its own directory and parent barriers up to that base.

requiredFindings.finding: The creating invocation's 'authoritative budget' is asserted but no owner issues one before an installation exists, and nothing bounds the ancestor walk, tree validation or P0 dependency construction.
requiredFindings.required: Name the budget owner for a pre-installation creating invocation and what it bounds, or state explicitly that creation is bounded by a fixed manifest rather than a shared budget.

requiredFindings.finding: Creating missing fixed ancestors is a durable side effect that survives a failed attempt, so 'I absent' does not imply 'no filesystem effect'. The disposition table reads as though nothing remains.
requiredFindings.required: Record the surviving-ancestor case and correct that row.
